label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
I’ve been seeing the conversation around Kavya’s post, and I want to respond directly rather than let people fill in the blanks.

Kavya and I are both in Foundry91 Cohort 4. We did demo day in March, and she’s been a real friend to me. Before demo day, she stayed with me till 1 a.m. in our Koramangala office, helping fix a mess with our Razorpay webhook. I haven’t forgotten that, and I respect her a lot.

Here’s what happened with the hiring. We posted a backend developer opening on DabbaDost’s LinkedIn page and Instahyre on 14 September, open to anyone. One person applied on 19 September; the second came through as a referral from him about two weeks later. No one from my side DM’d either of them. We offered 22% above their current CTC—not 40%—and both joined on 3 November. I’m saying the number plainly because I don’t want “40%” to keep circulating as fact.

On the ESOP point: we do have a small pool. It’s been on paper since January. We didn’t promise something that doesn’t exist.

But I also need to own where I got this wrong. I knew from day one where they worked. I should have called Kavya before making the offers, not after the second one was accepted. Instead, I WhatsApped her afterwards, and she didn’t reply. I wish I’d handled that conversation earlier and in person. That part is on me.

Kavya, this isn’t a fight or an attempt to rally people to my side. I’m sorry I didn’t give you a heads-up. You’ve shown up for me before, and I should have shown you the same consideration. I’d rather talk to you than argue through posts and comments.

We’re 11 startups in one cohort, hiring from the same small pool in HSR and Koramangala. This will happen again unless we agree on a simple norm: if you’re interviewing someone from another batch company, give that founder a heads-up before making an offer. Not permission. Just a heads-up, so there are no surprises.

I’m open to coffee or a call this week, whenever you’re comfortable. No pressure.
